purpose: Non-admission discovery of US observed severe-storm footprints, wildfire building damage and fuel vegetation data for distinct OpenCatastrophe hazard and validation use cases; model use, rights and retrieval are not approved.

entries.name: NOAA NCEI Event Footprint Catalog (EFC) 2026
entries.provider: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information
entries.spatial_scope: All 50 US states and selected US territories, with sensor- and hazard-specific availability
entries.temporal_scope: Tornado footprints January 2010 onward; hail footprints October 2020 onward; launched 2026 and refreshed about daily
entries.resolution_or_granularity: Event-specific GeoJSON and CSV footprint polygons, metadata and narratives; approximately 1 km source gridding for hail, assessment-derived paths for tornadoes
entries.note: Product lineage is NOT independent of NOAA Storm Events Database, NWS Damage Assessment Toolkit (DAT) and MRMS hail estimates, which may also contribute to previously registered NOAA/SPC data. DAT/Storm Events damage-path geometry and MRMS hail-polygon geometry are distinct source measurements and assumptions, not certified parcel-level damage. NOAA does not archive old catalog updates; freeze exact retrieval UTC, hazard, event/date, source version, bytes and SHA-256 before a reproducibility claim. No published API authorization is assumed.

entries.name: CAL FIRE Damage Inspection (DINS) Data
entries.provider: California Department of Forestry and Fire Protection (CAL FIRE)
entries.spatial_scope: California State Responsibility Area (SRA), inspected structures inside or within 300 feet of mapped wildfire perimeters
entries.temporal_scope: Incident-based mutable public database; provider portal updated 2026-10-21
entries.resolution_or_granularity: Structure-level inspection and damage-state attributes; portal offers ArcGIS GeoServices REST, CSV, GeoJSON, GeoPackage and other geographic downloads
entries.note: Provider documents affected/minor/major/destroyed/inaccessible/no-damage categories and reports survey/access limitations. Inspected structures are NOT a complete control sample of unburned buildings; absence from DINS must never imply no loss. Field-observed addresses and parcel/APN spatial joins can be uncertain; do not import or publish address-/parcel-level personal or policy data without a separate privacy decision. Portal states Creative Commons Attribution and no public-use restrictions, but exact resource reuse, citation, snapshot date and model semantics still require review.

entries.name: LANDFIRE 2025 vegetation and fire fuel products
entries.provider: LANDFIRE / USGS and US Forest Service
entries.spatial_scope: United States; product/region coverage varies for CONUS, Alaska, Hawaii and insular areas
entries.temporal_scope: LANDFIRE 2025 update with phased releases during 2026; CONUS full-extent update announced 2026-10-27
entries.resolution_or_granularity: Product-specific fire-behavior fuel rasters, canopy cover and height, fuel disturbance, seasonal fuels and vegetation classifications; region/resolution vary
entries.note: Source is a versioned FAMILY of modelled vegetation/fuel products, not a single observed wildfire, loss dataset or homogeneous global coverage. Select an exact named layer (e.g. FBFM40 or canopy height), US region, release, resolution, classification, observation vintage and byte identity before any research sample. Do not conflate fire fuel hazard potential with empirical burned area or building losses; model dependencies and reuse terms must be independently reviewed.
